questions.stem: A length is measured as 5.3 cm, correct to 1 decimal place. What is the lower bound?
questions.explanation: Rounded to 1 decimal place, the error interval is $\pm 0.05$. Lower bound $= 5.3 - 0.05 = 5.25$ cm. Any value from 5.25 up to (but not including) 5.35 rounds to 5.3.

questions.stem: A mass is given as 60 kg, rounded to the nearest 10 kg. What is the upper bound?
questions.explanation: Rounded to the nearest 10, the error interval is $\pm 5$. Upper bound $= 60 + 5 = 65$ kg. The actual mass satisfies $55 \leq m < 65$.

questions.stem: A rectangle has length $l = 8.4$ cm and width $w = 3.2$ cm, both measured to 1 decimal place. To find the maximum possible area, which bounds should you use?

options.text: Upper bound of $l$ $\times$ upper bound of $w$
Lower bound of $l$ $\times$ lower bound of $w$
Upper bound of $l$ $\times$ lower bound of $w$
Lower bound of $l$ $\times$ upper bound of $w$

questions.explanation: For the maximum area, use the largest possible values for both length and width. This means upper bound of length $\times$ upper bound of width.

questions.stem: A value is 4.7, correct to 1 decimal place. Which inequality represents the error interval?
questions.explanation: The lower bound is 4.65 (included, since 4.65 rounds up to 4.7). The upper bound is 4.75 (excluded, since 4.75 would round to 4.8). So $4.65 \leq x < 4.75$.

questions.stem: To calculate the minimum value of $\frac{a}{b}$, you should use:

options.text: Lower bound of $a$ divided by lower bound of $b$
Upper bound of $a$ divided by upper bound of $b$
Lower bound of $a$ divided by upper bound of $b$
Upper bound of $a$ divided by lower bound of $b$

questions.explanation: To minimise a fraction, make the numerator as small as possible (lower bound of $a$) and the denominator as large as possible (upper bound of $b$).

questions.stem: A distance is 200 m, correct to the nearest 10 m. What is the lower bound?
questions.explanation: Rounded to the nearest 10, the error is $\pm 5$. Lower bound $= 200 - 5 = 195$ m.

questions.stem: A speed is calculated using $\text{speed} = \frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}$. Distance is 100 m (to nearest metre) and time is 12.5 s (to 1 d.p.). What are the bounds needed for the maximum speed?

options.text: Upper bound of distance and upper bound of time
Lower bound of distance and lower bound of time
Upper bound of distance and lower bound of time
Lower bound of distance and upper bound of time

questions.explanation: To maximise speed (a division), use the upper bound of the numerator (distance = 100.5 m) and the lower bound of the denominator (time = 12.45 s).
